abstract.para: After a disaster has occurred, replace any broken hardware (if necessary). Then boot the &rear; recovery system and start the recovery installer with the rear recover command, using either the repaired machine (or a tested, identical machine that can serve as a replacement for your original system). Either on the original machine after replacing any broken hardware, or on an identical machine that replaces the original machine

listitem.para: A recovery system was created on the original machine.
The recovery system is available on a bootable recovery medium.
The replacement machine has identical hardware to the original machine.

topic.para: Perform this procedure on the replacement machine:

step.para: If necessary, replace any broken hardware.
Boot the replacement machine from the recovery medium.
Start the recovery installer with the -D option to enable verbose mode and debug mode:
This command performs the following steps:

listitem.para: Restores the disk layout, including partitions, file systems and mount points.
Restores the system files and user files from the backup.

step.para: After the recovery process is finished, check whether the system was successfully re-created and can serve as a replacement for the original machine in the production environment.
If the checks are successful, add the replacement machine back to the production environment.
